# Glider PRO 1.0.4 — shipped-house inventory (generated)

22 `.binhex` house files in `GliderPRO/Houses/` (the directory also holds 15
`.mov` demo movies, which are not houses). Every number below is measured from
the decoded BinHex payload; the `author` column is the only exception — it comes
from the credits in `GliderPRO/README.md:7-13`. Derived columns (dark, no-floor,
no-ceiling, structure, links, reachability) apply the original C rules, cited
per section below.

`data fork B` == 866 + 348 * `rooms` for 21 of the 22 houses. `Sampler.binhex`
is the exception: 1564 bytes for 2 rooms where the struct math gives 1562, i.e.
2 trailing bytes past the last `roomType`. A loader must therefore treat the
room count as `nRooms` from the header (offset 864) and tolerate slack at the
end of the fork rather than deriving the count from the file length. `firstRoom`
(offset 862) is in range for all 22 houses, so the game's clamp-to-0 fallback
(House.c:196 `GetFirstRoomNumber`) never fires on the shipped corpus.

## Backgrounds and embedded resources

Built-in backgrounds are PICT 2000 (`kSimpleRoom`) .. 2017 (`kStars`);
`kUserBackground` is 3000 and `kUserStructureRange` is 3300, so user art
>= 3300 is "outdoor" (non-structure) unless `bounds`&32 says otherwise
(Room.c:763 `IsRoomAStructure`).

For a user-art room the wall/floor/ceiling bits come from `room.bounds >> 1`
when `bounds` != 0, else from the house's own `bnds` resource for that PICT ID
(Room.c:937 `GetOriginalBounding`, which yields 0 — fully enclosed — and raises
a yellow alert when the resource is missing). 155 rooms across 7 houses
(Castle o' the Air 55, Rainbow's End 30, Slumberland 24, Land of Illusion 21,
Demo House 10, Leviathan 9, The Asylum Pro 6) take that fallback path, and every
one of them does have a matching `bnds` resource, so the boundsCode-0 default
never actually fires on the shipped corpus. `bnds` bit order is
left=1, top=2, right=4, bottom=8, each from one `Boolean` byte.

Sound triggers can outlive their sounds: Teddy World places 11 `kSoundTrigger`
objects pointing at `snd ` 3000 but ships no `snd ` resources at all, and In The
Mirror has two triggers on ID 10000 while shipping only 3001 and 3002. The
original silently drops those hotspots (`LoadTriggerSound` returns -1).

## Design metrics

`dark` = `GetNumberOfLights() == 0` (Room.c:970). Note the fall-through: for
`kDirt` (2011) rooms the background contributes a light only when all eight
tiles are 0, but a non-lit `kDirt` room still counts its window/lamp objects,
because the C code only skips the object loop when `count != 0`.

## Link integrity

"Link slots" = objects carrying a `(where, who)` pair: the six linkable
transports (0x33-0x36, 0x3F, 0x40) in `data.d` and the eight switches/triggers
(0x41-0x48) in `data.e`. `kSoundTrigger` (0x49) is deliberately excluded — its
`data.e.where` is a `snd ` resource ID passed straight to
`GetResource('snd ', id)` (ObjectAdd.c:499 defaults it to 3000; ObjectRects.c:926
→ Sound.c:265 `LoadTriggerSound`), not a room address.

`where` is `MergeFloorSuite(floor + kNumUndergroundFloors, suite)` =
`suite*100 + floor + 8` (Link.c:34, biased by the callers at Link.c:277 and
House.c:788); decoding for version >= 0x0200 is `suite = where/100`,
`floor = where%100 - 8` (Link.c:41 `ExtractFloorSuite`). `where` == -1 is "never
linked" (the value ObjectAdd.c writes on creation) and `who` == 255 is "no target
object chosen". `where` == -100 decodes to suite -1 == `kRoomIsEmpty`, i.e. a
slot pointing at no room; all 165 such slots corpus-wide also have `who` == 255,
so they are simply unlinked, and "hard dangling" excludes them. `resolved` +
`dangling` == `where`!=-1. The single `who` >= 24 entry is CD Demo House room 72
slot 22 (kMailboxRt, `where` 2109, `who` 35) — an object index past
`kMaxRoomObs`, which the original would read out of bounds.

Note that C's `/` and `%` truncate toward zero while Python floors; the only
negative `where` values in the corpus are -1 and -100, for which the two agree,
but a port must use truncating division to stay bug-compatible.

## Connectivity census

Counts of *adjacent room pairs* (grid neighbours that both exist). Grid
convention: east = `suite`+1, north = `floor`+1 (Room.c:562 
`GetNeighborRoomNumber`). "2-way" means both sides of the shared edge are
passable, "1-way" exactly one, "walled" neither. Horizontal passability is
`leftThresh`/`rightThresh` != wall-limit *or* a wall-ignoring object in the
room (kDoorInLf/kDoorExLf/kWindowInLf/kWindowExLf on the left,
kDoorInRt/kDoorExRt/kWindowInRt/kWindowExRt on the right — ObjectRects.c:799-868,
Interactions.c:572 `CheckEscapeLeft`). Vertical is `topOpen`/`bottomOpen`, plus
the kDirt tile escapes (Interactions.c:244, :378), kManhole's kIgnoreGround, and
the presence of a staircase object. "unpaired" up-stairs = a kUpStairs with no
kDownStairs in the room to the north (HouseLegal.c:961 `CheckForStaircasePairs`),
and vice versa.

## Static reachability

Edge set for the walk: the four grid neighbours that are passable in the sense
above, *plus* each linked transport (kMailboxLf/Rt, kFloorTrans, kCeilingTrans,
kInvisTrans, kDeluxeTrans) whose `where` != -1 **and** `who` != 255 — the game
only installs a transport hotspot when `who` != 255 (ObjectRects.c:751-895).
`components` are of the undirected graph; `BFS-reachable` and `max hop` are on
the directed graph. This is a static over-approximation: it ignores whether a
kDeluxeTrans starts switched on (`data.d.wide & 0x0F`), whether the glider has
the energy/bands to survive the trip, and one-shot triggers.
